title: Your Agent's Biggest Lie: "I Searched the Web" — Rafael Levi, Bright Data
talk_summary: A Bright Data vendor talk arguing that agents silently fabricate results when web fetches are blocked (CAPTCHAs, Cloudflare AI Labyrinth, empty pages) because LLMs are trained to please, and that the fix is giving agents real, unblocked web-access tools (search, scrape-as-markdown, remote browsers) plus explicit failure reporting. The only genuinely transferable engineering lessons are the failure-mode diagnosis, the 'LLM builds a parser, script runs it' token-saving pattern, and tool-subset loading to avoid context flooding.

takeaways.technique: Treat silent tool failure as a first-class defect: require explicit 'blocked/empty' reporting instead of letting the model improvise
takeaways.what_they_do: Diagnoses that when a fetch returns a CAPTCHA or empty page, the agent doesn't surface the error and instead substitutes training-data guesses or fabricated citations, producing invisible failures with no warning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: There's no error, no warning, just the wrong answer... It will try to make up something, and this is where the most of hallucinations come from.
takeaways.numbers: claims ~60% of ChatGPT citations don't resolve; 20% of web blocked to AI crawlers by Cloudflare

takeaways.technique: LLM writes a parser once, deterministic script runs it over N pages
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of sending each page's HTML through the LLM, have the agent generate a reusable parser/script and execute it over the whole batch, so tokens are spent once on authoring rather than per item.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Don't parse with LLM. LLM builds a parser and then the script runs it.
takeaways.numbers: claims ~99% token savings on parsing 10,000 pages

takeaways.technique: Load only the tool subset needed, not the full tool catalog
takeaways.what_they_do: The MCP exposes 66-69 tools but the speaker says to load only the 2-3 relevant ones per task, because dumping all tools floods the context with irrelevant schemas.

takeaways.technique: Scrape-as-markdown to strip HTML before the model sees it
takeaways.what_they_do: A fetch tool converts pages to markdown so the model doesn't burn tokens on HTML tags and boilerplate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It can send a curl to any URL and get just the markdown without HTML tags. So, you're not wasting tokens on parsing the HTML.

takeaways.technique: Batch API for many queries in one call
takeaways.what_they_do: A batch search tool accepts ~100 keywords and returns 100 results in one request, scaling without per-item round trips.

takeaways.technique: Publish a 'skills' page an agent can read to learn a procedure
takeaways.what_they_do: Bright Data hosts a page that teaches any agent how to build a scraper/pipeline with the right APIs, so the agent fetches instructions on demand rather than carrying them in every prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can take any agent, tell it to go here, and this page will teach it on how to build a scraper.
